findings.claim: F6 reproduction is explicitly acknowledged as untested, yet the rmcp candidate is committed to 'adapt', giving Plan no ordering signal between reproduction and binding work
findings.evidence: cand-003 risks: "Cross-principal session consequence is untested"; the F6 section states "If confirmed, bind all session operations to verified owner" and "This is a proposed fixture composition, not an already passing test." The verdict 'adapt' pre-commits to the post-confirmation work without a precondition.
findings.suggested_fix: Either mark cand-003 'pending' until the JWT-fixture reproduction runs and reports, or split the candidate into cand-003a (reproduction harness) and cand-003b (binding work, conditional). Plan must not be able to schedule binding work before reproduction.

findings.claim: G7-A is listed in gaps_addressed but no candidate has an adopt/adapt verdict; only cand-004 is 'reference', leaving the Plan stage without a concrete option for remote identity issuance
findings.evidence: cand-004 verdict='reference', and the only G7-A entry in build_required has capability_gap_id='REMOTE-RECEIVER-INVENTORY' — a blocking input. The analysis text says "Spec can define the common boundary and explicit unresolved receiver records without claiming deployment readiness," but the candidate set advertises nothing that Plan can directly author against.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'policy-config' or 'identity-policy' candidate (verdict: adopt/adapt) covering issuer/audience/algorithm/JWKS-freshness/role-attenuation policy on top of jsonwebtoken, so Plan has a concrete scope even when the receiver inventory is still pending. The receiver gap is a separate input, not a substitute for a policy component.

findings.claim: HTTP client version incompatibility for oauth2-rs is flagged but unresolved, and the chosen version conflicts with UAR's existing 0.13.4 pin
findings.evidence: cand-004 evidence cites oauth2-rs's optionalReqwest='^0.12' (research receipt) and the analysis says "Its built-in reqwest boundary must be reconciled with UAR's two HTTP-client versions; use an existing appropriate client or explicit adapter, not a wholesale transport upgrade." UAR already pins reqwest_mcp 0.13.4 and an application client at 0.12. The '0.12 application client' choice is never made explicit, and ^0.12 will not match a 0.13.4 deployment.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the target reqwest version (0.12) and the file path that will absorb the oauth2-rs HTTP trait impl, or mark cand-004 'reject' until the receiver is named. A third client version would be a 'no-new-service/no-new-stack' smell that needs an OpenSpec proposal.

findings.claim: G7-B secret storage authority is asserted as 'existing' but no candidate covers keyring/vault/KMS, so the credential-exposure path is a missing category of solution
findings.evidence: "use existing secure-storage authorities for credential bytes and refresh tokens." No candidate in the eight covers a secure-storage abstraction. build_required lists G7-B 'credential-exposure projection' as a need whose why_no_candidate is "Library secret wrappers cannot define policy" — but no candidate even establishes a storage wrapper to wrap.
findings.suggested_fix: Either reference the specific project module that owns credential storage (e.g., UAR's keyring integration) and cite its path, or add a build_required entry 'G7-B secure credential storage adapter' with capability_gap_id so Plan can author a storage abstraction explicitly.

findings.claim: 60-second nbf leeway is described as 'current explicit' but the value is not cited to source code and the term 'library leeway' is non-standard
findings.evidence: "Keep the current explicit 60-second library leeway visible in acceptance; changing it requires a deliberate contract." jsonwebtoken's parameter is named 'leeway' (Duration) and defaults to 0; if 60s is a UAR configuration it is at /Users/gqadonis/Projects/prometheus/universal-agent-runtime/src/uar/security/verifier/mod.rs (cited for nbf) but the leeway value is not pinned to a line.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the specific line in the verifier where leeway=60 is set (or note that it is the library default of 0 and 60s is a recommended upper bound), so Plan can preserve or change it deliberately and acceptance can assert the actual value.

findings.claim: cand-007 (Codex/Claude SDK) is 'reference' with no concrete comparison anchor, leaving Plan without measurable harness-comparison criteria
findings.evidence: cand-007 verdict='reference', evidence cites official docs for thread/turn/item and approval/interrupt; risks warn "Documentation comparison is not a reason to rewrite unrelated adapters" but no specific field is named as the comparison anchor. F1/F5 acceptance scenarios will be hard to assert against an unbounded reference.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the two or three interface fields (e.g., turn ID, approval ID, interrupt classification) that the comparison covers, or drop cand-007 as out-of-scope since the analysis says local adapters remain authoritative anyway.
